title: Corpse Princess
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Reanimated corpses called Shikabane walk the earth, and the Kougon Sect of a Shingon esoteric Buddhist school fights them with 'Corpse Princesses', undead girls bound to monks by contract (Yen Press blurb via AniList and MU). One of them, Makina, is told that destroying 108 Shikabane will bring her to Heaven (review). A 23-volume horror-action series.
life_message: It asks whether a person can keep their humanity while being used as a weapon.

content.note: Reviewer calls volume 1 a gorefest with limbs flying in every fight; MU Violence, Gun/s and Zombie Hunter categories.
Creepy horror the reviewer found too much; Horror genre on AniList and MU.
Fan service 'here and there' and a somewhat perverted monk (review); MU partial nudity, sexual innuendo; MangaDex suggestive.
Regret and grief over death (MU Regret, Death of Loved One/s).

dominant: Buddhist sect versus undead; keeping humanity; institutions using people

frames.aligns: Makina's will to keep her humanity; critique of using persons as tools.
frames.concerns: Salvation earned by 108 kills; necromantic contracts; gore.
Undead and contract magic treated as holy work.
Works-based heaven via another religion; graphic gore.

frames.aligns: Questions about the soul worth discussing.
frames.concerns: Buddhist sect's heaven by kill count; gore.
Demons, curses and undead pacts throughout.

frames.aligns: Exposes an institution's cynical use of girls.
Shows salvation-by-works bargains as hollow (review doubts sect).
Good and evil drawn with moral weight.

frames.concerns: Gore; why only girls are used is unexplained (review).
Undead magic; other-faith paradise; fan service.

frames.aligns: Karma and liberation imagery; righteous fighting.

frames.concerns: Killing as the path; sect shown as insincere.

frames.aligns: Skepticism of a cynical religious order.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Violent combat duty; contracts bind girl and monk.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Sect rules and contracts govern the princesses.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Monks command undead girls; a sect hierarchy.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Shingon esoteric Buddhism frames the world.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Fighting to survive and reach Heaven.

folkways.japan: Shingon esoteric Buddhism and the number 108 (worldly desires) draw on Japanese Buddhist tradition, used here as dark-fantasy setting.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer reads the humanity theme through events; no comment on preachiness.
delivery.note: The sect's motives are questioned through the plot, per one review of volume 1.

winners_losers: Makina's fight to stay human gains sympathy; the sect's use of girls as disposable tools is cast in doubt.
to_verify: How the Buddhist sect is portrayed across 23 volumes.
